final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That narrowing is substantively correct as far as it goes: aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and an 8% rollout with rollback support operational readiness, not policy satisfaction. But the governing compliance predicate remains unmet on the present record. Admissible evidence shows a material unresolved limitation in a named launch use case, continued exposure of that use case in the initial cohort, and no approved risk acceptance. The policy and provided policy text both require disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch; they also state that rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. Because the record still lacks evidence that disclosure has actually been made, this is not merely a caveated-compliance case. The caveat itself is the unresolved compliance requirement.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required model-card or launch disclosure for the tax filing assistant limitation is in place before launch.
The affected tax filing assistant segment remains below target on deduction eligibility explanation and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The only risk-acceptance record is an incomplete draft with no approver and no explicit treatment of tax filing assistant exposure.
Rollout controls, staged exposure, monitoring, and rollback do not satisfy the policy predicate because they do not exclude the affected use case and are not paired with approved risk acceptance.
